title: The Clergyman's Conjecture for anti-k-naccis
statement:
Let $X_n$ be the sequence of anti-$k$-naccis, defined as sums of $k$ consecutive missing numbers. A sequence is **$k$-automatic** when its base-$k$ value sequence can be generated by a finite automaton. **The Clergyman's Conjecture.** The difference

$$
X_n-(k^2+1)n
$$

is $k$-automatic. This conjecture proposes a uniform automatic description for all anti-$k$-naccis; the paper presents it as an evident pattern but does not establish it in the supplied text.
source_name: Wieb Bosma, Rene Bruin, Robbert Fokkink, Jonathan Grube, Anniek Reuijl and Thian Tromp, “Using Walnut to solve problems from the OEIS”, arXiv:2503.04122 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.04122

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).
